messages.subject: anova df
parts:
Hi Phil,

I thinkg there are related questions to this topic, but not exactly what I'm looking for, so I start a new one.

I run the anova test for two set of items: they have the same n. of obs (1686), but the first has 9 items, the second is a sub-sample with 7 items. The two are fitted with gpcm: y <- mirt(frscores, 1, itemtype='gpcm') and y2 <- mirt(frscores2, 1, itemtype='gpcm')

When calling anova(y2, y) the results are:

      AIC     AICc    SABIC      BIC     logLik       X2       df p
1 26150.8 26156.60 26304.02 26520.05 -13007.400                    
2 19797.0 19800.51 19916.42 20084.79  -9845.499 6323.802 77271025 1

The df seem huge. While if I compare  x <- mirt(frscores, 1, itemtype='rasch')  and y <- mirt(frscores, 1, itemtype='gpcm') with anova(x, y) where the two models have the same set of items (9) the df are 8, with p=0. 

Could you please tell me what's wrong? Is there maybe another GoF test I could run instead?

thank you very much for your help!

Best,
Olivia

parts: Hi Aiden,

On Tue, May 13, 2014 at 5:20 AM, Aiden Loe <loeba...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Phil, 

I thought I might just continue on this thread as this is a similar topic. 

I ran an anova between two models and below was this result. 
I was wondering if the p-value is based on the difference in the logLik value or the X2 value between the two models. I would really appreciate it if you could explain the difference in this two methods. I have seen some papers using logLikelihood ratio while others have use the chi-square to differentiate between the models. How are they different in the MIRT context?

The X2 value in statistical theory is based on the -2 * the log-likelihood difference; or just the ratio of the likelihoods. Some models can construct the overall model fit as a function of the maximized likelihood, so the two become approaches become identical. But the likelihood ratio approach is what is the fundamental approach to nested model comparisons.
And also, how if I want to see the chi-square specifically for one of the models, what function can I use?

These are often not computed by default, since the observed data tables are too space to reliably compute the X2 model fit statistic (or G2). This is one of the reasons the M2 statistic was formulated. Hope that helps.

Phil
